production.note: US model years. First: Cadillac's release 'DETROIT – Cadillac today introduced the 2016 CTS-V' with its '2016 CADILLAC CTS-V PRELIMINARY SPECIFICATIONS'. Last: GM Authority (Jonathan Lopez, 14 October 2019): "Production of the high-performance 2019 Cadillac CTS-V variant ended back in April" (gmauthority-last-cts-v); no opened Cadillac page states the end year.

fuel.note: Inferred from the release's description of the supercharged petrol V8.

transmission.note: 'Hydra-Matic 8L90', a 'paddle-shift eight-speed, electronically controlled' automatic. The only transmission.

powerHp.note: 2016 launch rating. Quote: "640 / 477 @ 6400 (SAE certified)" (hp / kW). Edmunds, Cars.com and KBB list the 2016 car at 640 hp. Car and Driver's road-test panel agrees: "Power: 640 hp @ 6400 rpm" (cd-cts-v-2016).

weightLb.note: Weight-order step 2: Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision, 9 October 2026, docs/DATA_GUIDE.md); a measured weight of C/D's test car. Car and Driver road-test panel labelled '2016 Cadillac CTS-V' by the owner (the pasted panel has no title line), quote: "Curb weight: 4129 lb". Test car: "TRANSMISSION: 8-speed automatic with manual shifting mode" (the only transmission), "PRICE AS TESTED: $95,290 (base price: $84,990)"; the panel names the engine "supercharged and intercooled V-8" with "Displacement: 376 cu in, 6162 cc". The earlier provisional figure, 4,145 lb from Cadillac's table headed 'PRELIMINARY SPECIFICATIONS' (Edmunds agrees), is 0.4% higher; Cars.com and KBB give 4,134 lb. See discrepancies.

discrepancies.reason: Car and Driver's figure is the measured weight of its test car; Cadillac's 4,145 lb is from a table headed preliminary (repeated by Edmunds); Cars.com and KBB list 4,134 lb. All within 0.4%.
discrepancies.resolution: Owner decision, 9 October 2026: the Car and Driver road-test curb weight is used (docs/DATA_GUIDE.md, Weight step 2). 4,129 lb used; the earlier 4,145 lb was the provisional (preliminary) figure.
